text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Ahead of the first full meeting of the new World Trade Organisation in Singapore this week, Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer called an 11th-hour meeting of the 14 Cairns Group of agricultural free trade countries to discss tactics and a strategy for making farm trade reform a priority for the WTO. Page 1.

As part of the Federal Government's plan to make it easier for small businesses to raise capital, Industry Minister John Moore has come up with the idea of companies being able to raise share capital without issuing a full prospectus and operating with minimal reporting requirements. Moore has also engineered a proposal to have a second board on the Australian Stock Exchange. Page 1.

Federal Opposition spokesman on industry, Simon Crean, has called on the Government to adopt a Ministry for International Trade and Industry (MITI) approach to industry policy, the same policy which has steered Japan's post-war industry development. Crean said business needs a secure policy framework, based on more active, explicitly interventionist measures that would transcend the electoral process. Page 4.

WMC Ltd's board is expected to approve the development of the A$650 million Duchess phosphate development near Mt Isa this week. The move adds impetus to North Queensland's multi-billion dollar minerals processing investment boom and should see WMC's wholy owned HiFert fertiliser company as the leader in the Australian market. Page 23.

Figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics show compulsory superannuation contributions and solid gains on major investment markets have assisted in lifting the value of Australian managed fund assets by A$33 billion to A$329.7
billion in the twelve months to September 30. Page 23.

With plans for its 60 per cent-owned Frazers Creek sapphire mine to be in production by the end of the month, Perth-based Desertstone has started drilling prospective targets on it land in the Gawler Craton, South Australia, to back its NSW sapphire projet. Desertstone began drilling gold prospects last week, but also has 34 possible kimberlite pipes. Page 24.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the plunge of 144 points on Wall Street on Friday, after comments by US Federal Reserve Board chairman Dr Alan Greenspan, financial markets will open nervously this morning, unsure whether the effects of Greenspan's comments have ended. The upheaval spread to the other northern hemisphere markets, and also to Asia and Australia, yet Colonial State Bank chief economist Hans Kunnen says that while local markets will retain their weak tone today, this should be short-lived. Page 17.

While Helix Resources NL has its rich gold intersections at Area 223, the Prospect, Lake Everard in the Gawler Craton region of South Australia, it has strong connections with the diamond industry, with managing director Rob Mosig doing geochemical analyss for Maureen Muggeridge when she found the first diamonds in the Kimberley, and Helix chairman Ewin Tyler being the man credited with getting Australia's diamond industry off the ground. Page 17.

As Industry Minister John Moore publicly stated the Federal Government was considering a modern form of second-board trading as an attempt to assist small and medium sized businesses gain greater access to investment capital, an Australian Stock Exchange pokesman said while this could be less than a year away, it would not involve any lessening of trading standards. Page 17.

Wallis inquiry chairman Stan Wallis has signalled his report may call for a mega-regulator which could combine all prudential regulation, including Reserve Bank functions, into one agency. The mega-regulator model is strongly supported by National Austraia Bank Ltd and looks to be the most radical of the proposals for a new regulation structure before the inquiry. Page 19.

St George Bank has launched legal action in the New South Wales Commercial Tribunal under Section 86 of the Credit Act which allows a credit provider to be excused from penalties for breaches while not legally admitting fault. While it is not known why the bank is taking the action, the Bank will be entitled to keep interest payable on about 250,000 personal loan accounts if it is successful. Page 19.

The Retail Therapy report from national advertising agency J Walter Thompson says a full national deregulation of trading hours will help stimulate the depressed retail sector by allowing retailers to address the flow of consumer dollars to non-retail "enertainment" activities. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian financial markets are hoping for a recovery today after a disastrous session on Friday that saw A$10 billion wiped off the value of the local market. While Wall Street was expected to fall as much as 180 points following comments by US

Federal Reserve chairman Dr Alan Greenspan, its drop at the end of trading of 55.2 points has seen Australian market watchers predicting a turnaround on the domestic front sometime this week. Page 35.

Former AWA boss John Dougall is the new chief executive officer of Aristocrat Leisure Ltd, which in the five months since it went public and listed on the Australian Stock Exchange, has seen two-thirds of its board change and is now hoping to crack the large evada, US, slot machine industry. Page 35.

Futuris Corp Ltd has signed a five year employment deal with its chief executive Alan Newman that will see Newman issued with six million share options exercisable at just A$1.55 each. The deal is still subject to shareholder approval and a strict performance hurdle, yet Newman's options are already in the money at around A$840,000. Page 35.

Researchers at Melbourne's Victoria University of Technology found companies may not be justified in cutting dividend reinvestment plans (DRPs) which are a popular way for small shareholders to invest. The research suggests many excuses for companies to drop DRPs were unfounded. Page 35.

Melbourne's Smorgon family has lifted its veil of secrecy by releasing financial accounts for its A$1 billion steel business as a result of the recent transfer of the Smorgon Steel assets to a new entity, The Australian Steel Company Pty Ltd. (TASCO). Th change in attitude reflects the fact that under Corporations
Law, the asset transfer to a new structure has resulted in Smorgon Steel losing its exempt disclosure status. Page 37.

BHP chairman-elect Jerry Ellis has defended the decision to purchase US-based Magma Copper for A$3.2 billion, by saying investor judgement on the acquisition was premature. Ellis believes the acquisition is a sound investment and its merits will be revealed over time. Page 37.
THE AGE

Futuris Corp has signed a new five-year employment contract with its chief executive Alan Newman, in a deal that sees Newman issued with six million share options exercisable at just A$1.55 a piece, although the agreement is still subject to shareholder aproval and a stiff performance hurdle. Page C1.

The Australian sharemarket will open warily today after an up and down day on Wall Street on Friday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average Index of US shares fell 144.6 points on Friday night but was stopped and partly reversed by employment figures showing lwer-than-expected US economic growth. Page C1.

Federal Industry Minister John Moore said yesterday he had held talks with Federal Treasurer Peter Costello over the proposal of a second stock exchange board to help small and medium-sized companies raise capital. Moore said he believed Costello had reated positively to the proposal but agreements would have to be reached with the Australian Securities Commission. Page C2.

While the meeting of world trade ministers this week is expected to reach consensus on a wide-ranging work program aimed at preparing the ground for substantial negotiations from 1999, the World Trade Organisation meeting could face two unresolved dispute - US plans to bring the issue of labor standards before the WTO and the European Union's bid to lay down global rules for investment. Page C3.

Venture capitalism is regaining its good name as the gloom following the 1980s fades away. In the new climate, the Australian Development Capital Association is considering changing it name to include 'Venture' to raise the profile of venture capital in Australia, where an estimated A$2 billion is available for development capital investment, with only A$1.7 billion actually invested. Page C3.

Sculptor Laszlo Biro has shown it is possible to make a living out of being an artist, after joining forces with Carole Pemberton, who runs the consultancy and brokerage for artists, Creative Personal Design. Pemberton acts as a middlewoman between artists and architects, interior designers and landscape architects to incorporate artists' skills at the start of a project. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
